producing_commit.resolved_when: at process start, when Python bound the modules this run executed -- NOT at artefact assembly, which is a later tree
producing_commit.why_this_is_here: This run takes hours and the tree moves under it. A consumer that wants to publish these counts needs to know which code drew them, and no diff between two artefacts can supply that.

world_identity.what_this_identifies: the departure LEVEL the world was running at -- `year_level_anchor` for every year inside the published switching record, fitted and declared alike. Two runs sharing this digest ran over the same departure surface; two that do not are different worlds however close their timestamps, and no figure from one bounds a figure from the other.
world_identity.what_this_does_not_cover: the HOMES. `_published_departure_rates` is the observed switching record and does not know what houses this world contains, so a re-drawn housing stock cannot move this digest and provably has not: `39a192ce04c1eda8` spans the population of `3957ba848` and the population of this tree, which hold different homes. That question is the `homes` part beside this one, and this part alone is NOT the world.

homes.what_this_identifies: the HOME STOCK the world draws from -- 96 homes drawn through `net_new_acquisition.year_premise_stock`, the function a run's own homes come from, and then through the fabric physics, digested as every field of simulation.fabric_physics.FabricParameters. Two runs sharing this digest drew their homes from the same stock through the same physics; two that do not saw different houses, however close their timestamps and however well their departure levels agree.
homes.what_this_does_not_cover: WHICH homes a particular run drew. A run chooses its own seed, size and year mix, so two runs sharing this digest still hold different individual houses -- this says they came out of the same country, not that they are the same. It also covers only the FABRIC: a change to heating fuel, appliances or occupancy that leaves every thermal parameter alone does not move it -- that is the `demand` part beside this one -- and the departure LEVEL is a separate part with its own digest.

demand.what_this_identifies: the DEMAND the world's homes generate -- the same 96 probe homes as the `homes` part, each run through `premise_trace.generate_premise_trace` for 7 real days of the C1 archive from 2020-01-13, digested as half-hourly electricity and gas. Anything that changes what a home draws in that week moves it: appliances, their ownership and season, the boiler's own electricity, supplementary heat, the thermal solve, the archive itself.
demand.what_this_does_not_cover: what `fabric_demand_path` layers on top of the trace -- the comfort constraint from last year's bill, away days, life-event segments -- and anything that only shows outside a January week. It identifies, it does not estimate: no figure should be read off these homes.

payment_methods.what_this_identifies: the payment method each household pays by -- `generate_payment_method` over 400 fixed ids on both fuels, the one draw the ledger is paid by and the seam reports. Two runs sharing this digest billed the same households by the same method.
payment_methods.what_this_does_not_cover: how a method behaves -- failure rates, lateness and arrears are the payment events, not the method -- and it is not the departure level or the home stock, each of which is its own part.

book_identity.how_a_consumer_should_pair_this: Pair on `declared` and never on `realised_across_seeds`. The declared half is the book the run was given; the realised half is what the seed's own churn did to it, so two floors of the SAME book differ there by construction. A consumer that compared the counts would refuse every honest re-run.

what_this_is: The three-arm A/B re-run once per seed with ONLY the per-household elasticity assignment re-drawn. The spread below is the error bar on `selection_gbp` -- the figure the level-vs-selection split publishes.
redraw_key_means: the per-household elasticity assignment. Reached ONLY by households the value arm priced -- it sits behind an offered rate -- so the `except` half of this key is empty on this book and gets emptier as the arm prices more of it

redraw_scope.means: every household re-drawn -- the undecomposed floor, and the only mode whose spread bounds the published figure directly

symbol_resolution: read from `simulation.customer_events`'s own import statement, not written down here, so a rename disconnects this tool LOUDLY instead of silently returning a spread of zero

selection_depth_against_money.why_not: every one of the 33 priced accounts faces the same number of priced renewals (1) on this run, so depth has no variance here and cannot explain any -- the same degeneracy the seed-level regressors hit, one cut down

shape.verdict: a SWITCH between two states -- the sd is a state distance times a mixing rate, and the Gaussian sem prices the wrong unknown
shape.what_this_replaces: the Gaussian sem. With two states the family mean is `rate x low + (1-rate) x high`, so the mean's interval is the RATE's interval carried through -- and the rate's interval at this many draws is what more seeds actually buys.

selection_residual_shape.why_no_sem: this family is a SWITCH, not a spread: its 4 draws fall into two states £233.33 apart, each at most £0.00 wide (separation 233325098000.0), with the lower state drawn 1 of 4 times. A standard error prices one quantity wobbling about a mean; here the unknown is the RATE at which the switch fires, so the bound is that rate's exact 90% interval (0.013 to 0.751) carried through to the mean: £-115.11 to £57.24, which contains zero, so no sign is stated. No standard error and no seed count is published for it.

distance_to_a_sign.why_not: this family is a SWITCH, not a spread: its 4 draws fall into two states £233.33 apart, each at most £0.00 wide (separation 233325098000.0), with the lower state drawn 1 of 4 times. A standard error prices one quantity wobbling about a mean; here the unknown is the RATE at which the switch fires, so the bound is that rate's exact 90% interval (0.013 to 0.751) carried through to the mean: £-115.11 to £57.24, which contains zero, so no sign is stated. No standard error and no seed count is published for it.

how_to_read_this: If the spread is WIDER than the published `selection_gbp`, the level-vs-selection instrument cannot yet resolve the question being asked of it, and every reading built on it carries that caveat. That is a finding about the INSTRUMENT and not about the pricing arm -- it is not a cue to re-run until a seed agrees (R12).
